day: Saints Cornelius, Pope, and Cyprian, Bishop, Martyrs on Wednesday of week 24 in Ordinary Time
text:
There is something childish about the way we keep score. We offer one thing, grow frustrated when it is refused, then offer its opposite—and grow frustrated again. We want others to dance to our music, or at least to cry to our dirge. Either way, we want to move them, to prove something, to be right.

Jesus sees this restlessness in us, the way we judge and reject and judge again. But he does not scold. He simply points toward something steadier: Wisdom, he says, is proved right by her children—by what love actually produces, by what endures. Not by our arguments or our intensity or how cleverly we switch strategies. Saint Paul knew this too. He had seen people speaking in tongues and moving mountains through faith, yet something was missing. Without love, he said, it is all just noise.

On this feast of Cornelius and Cyprian, men who gave their lives rather than abandon what they believed, we might ask ourselves: what kind of love moves us? Is it the love that insists on being understood, that needs validation? Or is it the patient, kind love that does not keep score, that delights in truth without needing to win? Perhaps today we could notice one moment when we let go of proving ourselves right, and simply loved instead.
